subject: [PATCH v4 01/21] iomap: split iomap_iter() logic into iomap_iter_next()

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch splits the iomap_iter() logic into a new helper function called iomap_iter_next(). The purpose of this change is to prepare for an upcoming modification to use an in-iterator model, where the ->iomap_next() callback will be able to directly call the iomap_iter_next() function. This allows for more flexibility and simplification of code. Additionally, two new macros are introduced to generate boilerplate wrapper functions for ->iomap_next(). The patch does not introduce any functional changes, but rather a code-level refactoring.

reviews.author: Brian Foster
reviews.summary: reviewer noted that iomap_end() may not necessarily transfer the iomap_flags on failure, potentially leading to a folio batch leak, and suggested accounting for failures from either callback by adding error handling in iomap_iter()

reviews.author: Darrick Wong
reviews.summary: Reviewer Darrick Wong expressed uncertainty about the practical impact of the patch, questioning whether the issue being addressed is actually encountered in practice and requesting further investigation before merging into for-next.

reviews.author: Brian Foster
reviews.summary: Reviewer Brian Foster noted that the patch is likely not hitting any error paths in reality and questioned the analysis of a potential issue with startblock check in xfs_bmbt_to_iomap(), suggesting it's mutually exclusive with a populated batch due to earlier validation.
reviews.raw_body:
Sounds good to me, I'll post the current patch shortly.

I don't think anybody is actually hitting this in reality; it just came
from a Sashiko review. I had an LLM walk through and try and tell me
what error paths could lead to this in practice and it basically
narrowed it down to the startblock check in xfs_bmbt_to_iomap(). When
pressed further from there, it says this is mutually exclusive with a
populated batch in practice due to earlier validation at the time the
extents are read in from disk.

I'm not sure I trust the analysis with 100% certainty, but all in all it
seems like an unlikely or second order (i.e. memory corruption, etc.)
error scenario.

Brian

2026-07-28.patch_summary: This patch splits the iomap_iter() logic into a new helper function called iomap_iter_next(). This is done in preparation for changing iomap to use an in-iter model, where ->iomap_next() implementations can call iomap_iter_next() directly. The patch also introduces two macros, DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT() and DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT_END(), which generate boilerplate code for the new in-iter model. No functional changes are intended, but there is a minor difference on the error path of iomap_end().
